central_claim: Across the small published EMC record this repository happens to hold, the NR4A3 5' fusion partner separates two crude, unadjusted quantities and nothing more. (1) PROGNOSIS: pooling the two pathology series that print per-partner event counts (Agaram 2014 n=23, Huang 2023 n=50; 73 patients) gives crude during-follow-up disease-specific death of 7/15 with TAF15::NR4A3 against 6/58 with EWSR1::NR4A3 - a descriptive contrast that the larger contributing cohort's own multivariable model attributes to tumour size rather than to the partner. (2) RESPONSE: three to five TAF15 patients have received an antiangiogenic TKI in the sources examined and none is recorded as responding, which is a direction with no magnitude, since the Wilson upper bound on the TAF15 rate lies above the comparator arm's own point estimate in both analyses. (3) PREVALENCE: 28/154 = 18.2% of partner-assigned EMC across four series. Every count is a crude proportion with a Wilson interval; no adjusted, time-to-event or predictive quantity is estimated anywhere, and none of the counts is read from a primary TKI report - both response cohorts' per-arm denominators come from reviews.

blockers.finding: Two partner-stratified series held in this repository are excluded from the synthesis without being disclosed to the reader anywhere in the manuscript, and both cut toward the null. (a) SJOGREN 2003 (PMID 12598313 / PMC1868116, Am J Pathol, Goteborg): a peer-reviewed, fully-accounted, karyotyped series of 10 EMCs from 9 patients with partner counts 5 EWSR1 / 3 TAF15 / 1 TCF12. It is in the artifact as cohort `sjogren-2003-prevalence` with `pool: false`, and the artifact flags its own significance in a key literally named '⚠_a_fifth_series_EXISTS_and_is_refused_on_a_DIFFERENT_ground', noting it 'would have PASSED s2.1(1), (2) at patient level and (4)' and fails only s2.1(3). More damagingly, the artifact records that it reaches the OUTCOME question too and that '⛔ THE MOVE IT WOULD MAKE IS NAMED SO THAT NOT MAKING IT IS VISIBLE: its three TAF15 patients record no tumour-related death, which would pull the pooled TAF15 disease-specific-death arm DOWN'. None of that reaches the manuscript. The word 'Sjogren' appears in the manuscript exactly once, inside a §8 bullet counting which citation records carry a cache slug - a reader has no way to learn the series exists, what it contains, or why it was refused. §3.5 compounds this by writing 'The **two** excluded congress abstracts bracket the pooled estimate', as though only two prevalence exclusions exist. (b) SUEMITSU 2025 (PMID 40828003, Genes Chromosomes Cancer, 18 MSK-IMPACT patients), retrieved into this repository via an actual Europe PMC fetch and written up in the companion document §6 of this very manuscript cites: it reports a partner distribution (14/18 EWSR1, 2 TAF15, 1 TCF12, 1 FUS) and, verbatim, 'no statistically significant correlation was detected between OS and fusion subtypes'. The companion calls it '⭐ a third independent series failing to establish the partner as a prognostic factor'. It appears nowhere in the manuscript or in the pooled artifact, is absent from §3.2's 'full inclusion table' even as a context/excluded row (which is how Paioli 2021 and the two congress abstracts are handled), is absent from §3.4's count of the series that have tested the partner prognostically, and is absent from §6's falsifier #5, which asks for exactly this kind of third cohort as if none existed. Its FUS::NR4A3 case is also the concrete instance of the possibility §3.1 and §4.6 raise only hypothetically ('may include *FUS*, *TCF12* or untyped').

blockers.why_it_blocks: A synthesis that publishes an inclusion/exclusion table and calls it 'the full inclusion table' must show every candidate it refused, especially the ones it refused on contestable grounds and especially the ones whose data run against its own result. Here the two that are invisible are precisely the two that push the headline toward the null - one whose TAF15 arm has zero disease-specific deaths, one that tested OS by partner and found nothing. Both exclusions may well be defensible (s2.1(3) for Sjogren; MSKCC population overlap and no per-partner event counts for Suemitsu). The defect is not the exclusion, it is that the reader is never told either exists, while being told the table is complete. That is selective reporting on the face of the document, and it is the first thing a rival group holding those two papers will say.

p1s.finding: The paper's declared substitute for a heterogeneity model is not delivered where it matters. §2.5: 'The honest heterogeneity signal at this scale is the **range of per-cohort rates**, printed beside every pooled figure.' Neither results table prints one. The omission is largest exactly where it flatters the contrast: the secondary TKI analysis pools the sunitinib series' EWSR1 arm (6/8 = 75.0%) with the pazopanib trial's non-TAF15 arm (4/19 = 21.1%) into a single '37.0%' comparator - a 53.9-point spread the artifact computes and the manuscript never shows - so the reader sees 0% vs 37.0% rather than 0% vs {21.1%, 75.0%}. Similarly the pooled local-recurrence row ('4.3 pts ... no material separation') conceals a per-cohort direction flip: Agaram gives TAF15 28.6% vs EWSR1 6.2%, Huang gives 25.0% vs 28.6%. The paper devotes a whole flagged paragraph to the metastasis reversal and is silent about the recurrence one.

The prevalence pool sums exactly (16+46+8+50 = 120; 7+9+2+10 = 28; 5; 1; denominators 24+57+11+62 = 154) and the residues quoted in §4.3 (2, 1, 1, 5) reconcile with each series' n_tested. I attacked the verbatim quotations against the literature-cache branch and every one I could reach verified exactly: Bangerter's 'A medium throughput drug screen using 40 drugs was conducted with USZ20-EMC1 at passage 5', 'Both models independent of the NR4A3 fusion partner showed high sensitivity to carfilzomib', the 2012 hedge 'Even in EMCS the fusion-protein is unlikely to be related to sunitinib sensitivity' (PMC3534218), the 2014 counter-sentence 'Genotype/phenotype analyses support a correlation between response and EWSR1-NR4A3 fusion', and both §1.1 quotations plus 'Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, which is the first-line regimen used in STS, has low activity in this sarcoma subtype' - I initially believed this last one had no provenance anywhere and was about to report it as fabricated; the repository-wide grep instructed here saved me from a false accusation, since it is verbatim in origin/literature-cache:literature/bangerter-2023-emc-exvivo/PMC9813045.txt. I likewise tried to break Appendix A11's characterisation of Masunaga 2025 and could not: registry.citations.masunaga2025 exists in emc-clinical-registry.json with the matching PMCID, DOI, title, n = 171 and design 'retrospective national registry cohort'. Huang 2023's prevalence counts (46/9/2 with 1 unassigned over 58), the 78%->10 cm figure and the multivariable result are independently corroborated by the Europe PMC abstract, which I read myself. The estimand discipline is real rather than decorative: the metastasis pooling genuinely is label-matched not definition-matched and says so, the two readings are both printed, and the follow-up asymmetry is stated with its direction. The scope discipline also holds - I could not find a sentence anywhere in the document that asserts efficacy, safety, selectivity, a therapeutic window, clinical readiness or a treatment recommendation, and the prognosis/response separation is enforced consistently, including the correct refusal to let Huang 2023 touch the response analysis. My four blockers are all about what the prose says about the evidence, not about the evidence.
scope_note: All four blockers are refuted INFERENCES or misdescriptions, not refuted measurements. HR-B1 is a misdescription of the pooling method in the Abstract - the counts and intervals it reports are correct. HR-B2 is an over-strong inference from a correct zero-event count. HR-B3 is an over-attribution of an analysis to a source, contradicting the same document elsewhere; the Huang half of the claim is sound and the Paioli half is not. HR-B4 is non-disclosure of two excluded sources; both exclusions may be methodologically correct, so nothing computed is refuted - what is refuted is §2.3/§3.2's assertion that the reader has been shown the full inclusion table. Among the P1s, the §8 miscount (11 vs 12) and the stale method.not_used range ('2-19 patients and 0-10 events') ARE refuted measurements, both trivially checkable; the rest are refuted inferences or undisclosed limits.
